correctedState: Confirmed, with one corrected line reference and one added upstream cause. Nothing in the repo ever builds a `<channel>` element: `grep -rna '<channel' packages apps` over .ts/.tsx yields only unrelated CLI usage strings. The event text is delivered to the model raw. Chain: `packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:357-361` constructs `{ server: this.channelServer, text: boundedChannelText(text) }` from `params.text` alone — `meta` is never read, so the per-key attributes the page specifies (`channels-reference.md:229`) never enter the process at all; `packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:1082-1105` dispatches that full message to subscribers, so the slug is intact at the seam; `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2436` destructures `({ text })`, discarding `server`; `PiAgent.redirect` at `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7109` (NOT :7086-7095, which is `forceAbort`) sends `{ type: 'steer', message }`; `packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:4329-4333` passes it to `piSession.steer(msg.message)` unchanged. The plugin-monitor sibling at `SessionManager.ts:2420` is likewise unwrapped. Consequence, verified independently of the identifier: the model receives channel events indistinguishable from a user steer, cannot attribute an event to a source, and has no `chat_id`-style routing attribute, so a channel plugin whose `instructions` say 'Reply with the reply tool, passing the chat_id from the tag' describes a tag that never appears. The parity audit already grades this surface `partial` (`2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1764`) with R3 as the owning plan.
